info.name: SmartFix API v2
info.description:
Live API for SmartFix — Tecdia machine troubleshooting RAG. Updated post-meeting (2026-05-02) to cover worker domain sessions, machine category/significance fields, severity scoring on /query, and the new alerts API.

Server must be running locally on http://127.0.0.1:8000 (see README for `uvicorn` command).

Folders are organized in demo order — start at the top of each folder and work down.

request.description: Liveness probe. No auth. Returns `{status, version}`. Run this first to confirm the server is up.

Open a worker session by selecting an expertise domain. No email needed — the workstation is trusted by physical presence.

Allowed values for `domain`: `General`, `Manufacturing`, `Additive Manufacturing`, `Fabrication`, `Automation`, `Heavy Machinery`, `All Access`.

Sets cookie `worker_session` (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, 12h TTL). Postman captures the cookie automatically — subsequent requests in this folder will be treated as a worker.
Sends an unknown domain. Server rejects with 400 in the contract envelope: `{detail, code: 'invalid_domain'}`.

Run after `/auth/worker-session`. Returns `{authenticated, role: 'worker', domain, email: null, session_expires_at}`.

The frontend uses this as the single source of truth for the current user — never assume how the user authenticated.
Clears the worker session cookie + in-memory session. Returns `{ok: true}`.

Step 1 of magic-link login (managers/admins). Always returns 200 so attackers can't enumerate valid emails.

**Stub:** does not actually send mail yet. Awaiting Tecdia domain decision for Resend/SMTP.

Step 2 of magic-link login: user clicks the email link. Server validates the token, sets a session cookie, redirects to `/`.

**Stub:** accepts any token.

When there is no worker_session cookie, the stub returns the admin user. Returns `{authenticated, email, role: 'admin', domain: 'All Access', session_expires_at}`.

Flip `STUB_ROLE` in src/api.py to test alternate paths.

**Tip:** if you ran `/auth/worker-session` first, run `/auth/logout` to clear the worker cookie before hitting this.

Returns the list of machines available for the worker. Each machine includes `id`, `display_name`, `chunk_count`, `description`, `category`, `significance` (1–5), and `icon`.

Workers should only see machines whose `category` matches their domain (or all machines if domain is `All Access`). Admins see all machines.

Real RAG: retrieve → prompt → Groq → cited answer.

Response now includes:
- `severity_level` (1–5, LLM-assessed)
- `alert_score` (severity × machine_significance)
- `machine_significance` (echoed)
- `alert_fired` (bool — true if score ≥ ALERT_THRESHOLD, default 12)

For a factual query like this, expect low severity (1–2) and no alert fired.

item.name: POST /query — error code lookup (likely fires alert)

request.description:
Multi-step troubleshooting. Returns a structured procedure with page references.

INJECTION_MOLDING_MACHINE has machine_significance=5; if the LLM rates severity as 3+ (likely), alert_score ≥ 15 and `alert_fired: true`. Check `/admin/alerts` after this to see the auto-created record.

Demonstrates conversation memory. The bare question 'How do I fix it?' would be ambiguous on its own; with history, retrieval correctly pulls the E-06 chunk and the LLM answers with the full E-06 procedure.

Demonstrates the refusal discipline: the model declines to answer and explains that the documentation only covers the indexed machines.

Expected severity: 1 (informational). Expected alert_fired: false.

item.name: POST /query — domain access denied (run after worker-session=Manufacturing)

request.description:
Demonstrates domain-based access control.

Prerequisite: open a worker session with domain=Manufacturing (folder 1).

LASER_CUTTING_MACHINE has category=Fabrication. The Manufacturing worker is denied with 403 in the contract envelope: `{detail, code: 'access_denied'}`.

If you skipped the worker session, this request will pass through (admin/no-cookie callers are not gated).
600-character question. Pydantic rejects with 422 in the contract envelope: `{detail, code: 'validation_error'}`.
Admin view of /machines. Includes everything in the worker view (category, significance, description, icon) plus admin-only fields: `uploaded_at`, `uploaded_by`, `pdf_size_bytes`.

Multipart upload. Pick any PDF file in the `file` row before sending.

New form fields per v2 contract:
- `description` (string, optional) — shown on machine card
- `category` (string, optional, default 'General') — used for worker domain access control
- `significance` (int 1–5, optional, default 3) — business impact
- `icon` (file, optional) — enable the row to upload an icon

Returns 202 with a `job_id`; the test script captures it into the `job_id` collection variable so the next request works automatically.

Duplicate machine_id returns 409 in the contract envelope. Significance outside 1–5 returns 422.

Poll this every ~2 seconds after upload. Returns status across the lifecycle: queued → parsing → chunking → embedding → indexing → done. Stub progresses over ~10s for demo purposes (real ingestion takes longer).

Remove a machine and all its indexed chunks. Default target is the demo fixture HP-500 — change `machine_to_delete` variable to delete something else.

Real endpoint — actually deletes from ChromaDB and clears the machine's metadata.

List all alerts (newest first) plus the active alert threshold.

Alert records are auto-created by `/query` when `severity_level × machine_significance ≥ ALERT_THRESHOLD` (default 12).

Each alert: `{alert_id, machine_id, score, severity_level, machine_significance, question, answer_excerpt, email_notified, notified_at}`. Matches the shape rendered in the admin UI's Critical Fault Alerts panel.

Injects a synthetic alert into the in-memory store. Useful for verifying the email pipeline once it's wired (currently `email_notified` is a stub flag).

Returns 201 with the created alert record.
Clears the alert history. Maps to the 'Clear All History' button in the admin UI. Returns `{ok: true, cleared: <count>}`.
